blocks.title: Elementary Fermions: Strings, Planck Constant, Preons and Hypergluons
blocks.content:
Preons and Hypergluons 
Doron Kwiat
 
Mazkeret Batyia, Israel

blocks.title: Abstract
blocks.content:
Using real fields instead of complex ones, it is suggested here that the fer-
mions are pairs of coupled strings with an internal tension. The interaction 
between the two coupled strings is due to an exchange mechanism which is 
proportional to Planck’s constant. This may be the result of two massless bo-
sons (hypergluons) coupled by a preon (prequark) exchange. It also gives a 
physical explanation to the origin of the Planck constant, and origin of spin.

blocks.title: Keywords
blocks.content:
Fermions, Preons, Hypergluons, Strings, Real Fields, Planck Constant,  
Interference, Spin

blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content:
The Standard Model recognizes two types of elementary fermions: quarks and 
leptons. 
Mathematically, there are many varieties of fermions, but we will concentrate 
on Dirac fermions (massive), including neutrinos, leptons, neutrons, protons 
and their building blocks-quarks. Most Standard Model fermions are believed to 
be Dirac fermions. 
All Dirac fermions have mass and obey the Dirac equation.

blocks.title: Weyl and Majorana
blocks.content:
Weyl [6] showed that the massless Dirac Equation could be reduced to a 
two-component equation. The solutions of that equation are called Weyl spi-
nors, or Weyl fermions [6]. 
What is currently accepted is the following status. 
Weyl fermions are two-component spinors.  
Massive Dirac spinors can be written as combinations of left- and right-handed 
massless Weyl fermions. 
Another way of representing the massive Dirac equation found by Ettore Ma-
jorana [7].

pothesized by Ettore Majorana in 1937. The term is sometime
